# requireNonArray

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not an array.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonArray() — Returns the value after checking that it is not an array. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonArray<T>(
  value: T | unknown[],
  message: string = "Expected a non-array value."
): T;
```

`Array.isArray` is the whole test, so an array from another frame counts and an array-like object — `arguments`, a `NodeList`, `{ length: 0 }` — does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                | Type             | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                  | `T \| unknown[]` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-array value."` | `string`         | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with an array excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition              |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is an array. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonArray("abc"); // => "abc"
requireNonArray({ length: 0 }); // => { length: 0 }
requireNonArray([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonArray([1, 2, 3]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
